decisions.reason: The complete current primary report explicitly identifies the IBM uncertainty-avoidance finding in Hofstede’s Culture’s Consequences (1980), co-attributing the original items to its 2001 second-edition account. It tests that one finding in ESS2010, with one old anonymous target and one source-identified current target. Select the actually cited 1980 book for existing row410 instead of the shipped journal citation. This is repair of the existing replication-original binding, not evidence of a second empirical target: no journal/book sample or finding equivalence, independence, or priority is inferred. The 1980 journal body remains inaccessible after six recorded routes, so its relationship to the book remains an explicit limit. Different DOI/title alone does not justify an additional pair.

decisions.quote:
1. Items in the IBM questionnaire used by Hofstede for computing his original uncertainty
avoidance index (Hofstede, 1980, 2001)
(UAI-a) Please indicate the extent to which you personally agree or disagree with the following
statement: Company rules should not be broken—even when the employee thinks it is in the
company’s best interests:

     1. Strongly agree 2. Agree              3. Undecided             4. Disagree
     5. Strongly disagree

   (UAI-b) How long do you think you will continue working for this company?

     1. Two years at the most 2. From two to five years
     3. More than five years (but I probably will leave before I retire)                            4. Until I retire

   (UAI-c) How often do you feel nervous or tense at work?

     1. I always feel this way 2. Usually                  3. Sometimes
     4. Seldom 5. I never feel this way.

2. Items in the ESS 2010 used in this study to compute a 2010 uncertainty avoidance index for
European countries
Firstly, I am going to read out a list of statements about how you may have been feeling recently. For
each statement I would like you to say how often you have felt like this over the last two weeks.
Please use this card.
